target_customer: Film, TV and video production teams, later small teams producing marketing video
problem: Footage is scattered and hard to search, and editing and review are slow.
business_model: B2B SaaS per editor (Pro 25 USD per editor per month per a third-party summary)
product_category: AI video editor and media asset manager

founders.name: Luke Igel
founders.background_notes: YC page lists NASA JPL, SpaceX, Slack, CSM, KoKo.

competitors.name: Nova A.I. Video Analysis and Search
competitors.what: Indexes media libraries so scenes can be found by emotion, object, person or action

technical_complexity.rationale: Video indexing and search with integrations into editors; multimodal models were becoming available in 2023.

defensibility.rationale: Footage libraries create some lock-in but many video AI tools launched in 2023.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Adobe researched AI editing (Project Blink); no acquisition of Kino found.

market_need_then: Productions accumulate large footage libraries; the company says it grew out of bespoke deployments for productions (per a Nov 2026 launch summary).

branding.domain_note: Uses kino.ai, an exact .ai name; acquisition details not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful and confident, short direct headlines

branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN post for the standalone editor reported Nov 2026.

brand_strength.rationale: Many unrelated Kino brands (camera app, film distributor); no brand press found.

pivots.from: AI media manager for filmmakers integrating with Premiere and DaVinci Resolve
pivots.to: Standalone AI video editor shared by teams and coding agents
pivots.why: Company describes it as a rebuild of earlier bespoke deployments (per third-party summary)

outcome_analysis: Kino AI is active with four staff and a single listed founder. It started as a footage manager for film productions and in November 2026 launched a standalone agent-friendly editor. Aggregators show a small seed from Pioneer Fund and YC only, so funding is unverified. The outcome is too early to judge.
notes: Funding (about 500K from AAI Grant, Pioneer Fund, YC) is from aggregators only, unverified. Aggregators place the company in San Francisco and name Wesley Block as CEO, but the YC page lists only Luke Igel, so only he is recorded. YC lists Boston. Founded 2022 per aggregators.
